The debt‑service coverage ratio in month t is  

\[
DSCR_t \;=\dfrac{\text{FOI}_t}{\text{debt‑service}_t}
\]

and the covenant requires \(DSCR_t \ge 1.25\).

For a constant growth \(g\) applied every month,

\[
\text{NOI}_t=130\,(1+g)^{\,t-1} .
\]

The covenant is met whenever for every \(t=1,\dots ,12\)

\[
130(1+g)^{t-1}\ \ge\ 1.25\times\text{debt‑service}_t .
\]

Re‐arranging gives the bound

\[
(1+g)^{t-1}\ \ge\ \frac{1.25\,\text{debt‑service}_t}{130}\, \qquad
\]

For the periods 1–3, 4–6, 7–12 the right‑hand side becomes

\[
\begin{aligned}
\frac{1.25(80)}{130}=0.76925\\
\frac{1.25(110)}{130}=1.05884\\
\frac{1.25(140)}{130}=1.34615
\end{aligned}
\]

The most restrictive month is the first month that has the ratio above the level that will force \(g>0\); that is month 7.  
So the critical inequality for month 7 is

\[
(1+g)^6 \;\ge\;1.34615 .
\]

Taking sixth roots yields

\[
1+g\,\ge\;(1.34615)^{1/6}\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
g \;\ge\;(1.34615)^{1/6}-1 .
\]

Numerically

\[
(1.34615)^{1/6}=1.04817\;\Longrightarrow\;g\ge0.04817 .
\]

Thus the minimum constant monthly growth that will keep the DSCR above 1.25 in every month is about

\[
\boxed{0.048\,5\text{ (about }5.0\%\text{ per month)}} .
\]
